transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (CSM), Ava Soto (SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, AeroVista), Marcus Reid (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (VP Product), Omar Khalid (Security)
Shared links: deck (https://redwood.app/share/av-pilot-deck), pilot-cost-sheet (https://redwood.app/sheets/av-pilot-costs), security-portal (note: link sent after call)

Summary:
Quick sync to move AeroVista from discovery to a short pilot. Focus: runway readiness (capacity, autoscale), cost vs latency tradeoffs for their batch prefill and low-latency route, and security checklist for VPC/KMS. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot with a stress test and a guardrail for cost.

Topics:
- Current usage & cost pain points
- Latency SLOs for two routes (ingestion/batch vs interactive customer chat)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and fallbacks
- Security: KMS, audit logs, VPC peering, SOC2 artifacts
- Pilot scope, timeline, and success criteria

Action items (quick list - also in metadata): see action_items field
Questions raised:
- Can Redwood support warm cache prefill to reduce p99 for interactive route?
- What is the fallback behavior if dedicated pool hits capacity?
- How are billing spikes controlled during stress tests?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Short agenda: confirm pilot scope, infra checklist, and security next steps. We wanted to make sure we're aligned before we run the pilot.
[00:24] Lena (Head of ML): Thanks Maya. Yeah, we're trying to move faster but we had a surprise bill last month so we gotta be very careful about bursts. We like the econ suggestions you shared but need a little more concrete on the guardrails.
[00:40] Maya: Totally. We'll walk through a cost model and a burst policy. Ravi will show latency tradeoffs with quantization and batching after quick context.
[00:52] Marcus (Platform Eng): Quick context from our side: two main routes—one is back-office batch prefill that runs asynchronously (median 600 tokens, sometimes 2k), and the other is an interactive chat for customers (median 180 tokens). For the chat route we need p95 < 220ms ideally, p99 under 400ms.
[01:12] Ravi (SE): Okay good, so two different workload profiles. For batch we recommend higher batching + lower-cost quantized variants, for chat we want a lower-latency variant and smaller sequence optimizations. Redwood Dedicate — sorry, Redwood Dedicated — can help here if you want isolated pools.
[01:36] Priya (VP Product): We're leaning hosted first to move faster but open to Dedicated if latency consistently misses. The security team will want clarity on data residency and KMS.
[01:50] Omar (Security): Yeah, SAML SSO is baseline, plus we need an option for customer-managed KMS. Also SOC2 and audit logs. Do you have a sample network diagram for private deployments?
[02:05] Ava (Solutions Eng): We do, we'll drop the diagram in the portal. Redwood Private (VPC) supports customer-managed keys and peering; I'll include the template. Note: some names in the diagram were transcribed wrong in earlier docs, so double-check the subnet ids when you paste them in.
[02:26] Lena: That helps. On costs, last spike was mostly from repeated short chat calls during a product launch. Is there a way to throttle or cap token spend per route?
[02:40] Noah (CSM): We can set per-route quotas and burst caps, and also configure cache-prefill to reduce repeated token generation. We'll show an example config in the pilot.
[02:55] Marcus: Cache-prefill sounds promising. Does it maintain KV cache across sessions?
[03:04] Ravi: Yes, we do prefix caching and can persist hot KV segments for the interactive route. There's a tradeoff on memory and cost but p99 improves significantly. We'll run a microbenchmark.
[03:20] Speaker 1 (Customer, unclear): So if we prefill the cache, are we billed for the prefill tokens?
[03:26] Maya: Great question. Prefill does incur token-like compute cost but we can discount prefill in the pilot pricing or amortize across bursts. We'll show the math.
[03:38] [03:38] Ravi: Ok quick bench note — with our suggested quantization + batching for batch route we saw 3x cost reduction on similar workloads, for interactive with prefill p99 dropped ~45% in our tests but median latency only changes modestly.
[04:00] Priya: I'm concerned about fallbacks. If Dedicated pool reaches capacity during a campaign, what's the user-visible behavior? We can't have errors for customers.
[04:12] Ravi: We support automated fallback to a compatible hosted model variant in the same region — configurable policy: fail-open vs queue vs fallback. For customer-facing chat we suggest fallback with degraded but still workable variant, plus a circuit-breaker alert to your ops channel.
[04:31] Marcus: Ok, and will the fallback change cost drastically?
[04:36] Maya: It can; we can set a budget-based fallback where beyond a threshold we route to a lower-cost model. That preserves service while capping spend.
[04:49] Lena: For success criteria, we want: 1) interactive p95 < 250ms for 99% of test window, 2) batch throughput > X rps under our sample load, and 3) no security gaps during onboarding.
[05:05] Noah: We'll codify those as pilot KPIs and instrument with per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.
[05:13] Marcus: For the pilot traffic sample, what's the best format? We can share anonymized logs.
[05:19] Ravi: Logs with request/response token counts, sequence lengths, and timestamps are ideal — CSV or NDJSON. We'll scrub PII on our side too.
[05:30] [05:30] Priya: About billing spikes — could we run a controlled stress test to simulate a launch but with caps? We want to see behavior without risking real spend.
[05:40] Maya: Absolutely. Pilot plan: a staged stress test week 2 with a synthetic load that mirrors your peak, with a hard cap that we agree on. We can also do a dry-run in our staging with the same config.
[05:52] Omar: Security questions — KMS integration for Redwood Private, will keys ever leave our account?
[05:58] Ava: No, for customer-managed KMS we support envelope encryption where the root key stays in customer KMS/HSM, and Redwood holds an ephemeral wrapping key only. We'll provide architecture docs.
[06:12] Lena: Ok good. Any limitations on on-prem? We have a region with strict data handling but not fully air-gapped.
[06:20] Ravi: We support private deployments with controlled egress; for fully air-gapped there are more constraints but we have an on-prem package. We'll need to scope that separately — likely longer timeline.
[06:34] Speaker 2 (Customer): Are there specific SLAs for Dedicated? We need to present to procurement.
[06:40] Maya: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll attach the SLA draft in the follow-up. That will include typical credits and uptime thresholds.
[06:49] Priya: Can you also share a sample contract clause for model governance and deprecation? That's a blocker for legal.
[06:56] Maya: We'll include a sample governance clause and a model-rollout plan.
[07:04] Marcus: On instrumentation, does Redwood surface token-level cost on a per-request basis?
[07:09] Noah: Yes, Console shows token breakdowns and cost per route; we'll attach a screenshot in the pilot readout.
[07:18] Lena: Small nit: we had a bad experience with truncated transcripts in previous vendor demos, hope your logs are more reliable.
[07:25] Maya: Understood, we'll ensure full request/response logging for the pilot and ship a checklist.
[07:33] [07:33] Ravi: One more technical: quantization options — for batch we can use 8-bit quantization and medium quality, for chat a 6-bit config with lower vocab precision might be okay if p95 is still acceptable. We'll run against your median sequence lengths.
[07:50] Marcus: Cool. Can you show a quick example config for per-route quota?
[07:54] Ava: Sure — we have a snippet in the deck and the pilot-cost sheet will include an example. We'll push both after call.
[08:04] [08:04] Priya: Timeline — we want pilot start week of 2026-09-28, two weeks duration, then decision meeting the week of 2026-10-19. Can you confirm resources?
[08:16] Maya: We can commit SE time for kickoff and the staged stress test, CSM for weekly check-ins, and solutions eng for the KMS/network handoff. We'll lock time once we get the traffic sample and POA.
[08:29] Marcus: On the POA — procurement wants an estimate for a short-term reservation vs purely usage-based.
[08:35] Maya: We'll include both options in the pilot pricing: small reserved pool for predictable throughput and a usage-backed alternative.
[08:44] [08:44] Lena: Any concerns on our side about models getting deprecated during pilot? We update our prompts often and need model stability.
[08:52] Ravi: You can pin model versions in Redwood; we'll ensure the pilot uses pinned versions and alert on model deprecation windows.
[09:00] Omar: For audit logs, do you keep immutable logs for 90 days?
[09:05] Noah: Default retention is 30 days, enterprise options for extended retention and export to your SIEM. We'll add that to the security doc.
[09:16] Priya: Great. Let's recap next steps quickly.
[09:20] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood to send pilot pricing + SLA + sample governance clause (Maya) by 2026-09-22; 2) AeroVista to upload anonymized traffic sample (Marcus) by 2026-09-20; 3) SE microbenchmarks on median seq lengths (Ravi) by 2026-09-21; 4) Security artifact list and KMS approach confirmed (Omar) by 2026-09-23; 5) Pilot kickoff scheduled for week of 2026-09-28.
[09:50] Lena: That sounds good. Also please flag any config that will cause token-cost surprises.
[09:58] Maya: We'll highlight token-heavy paths and a recommended cost cap.
[10:05] [10:05] Ava: I'll also drop the VPC diagram and a trimmed runbook in the portal.
[10:12] Marcus: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:16] Maya: Thanks folks — we’ll follow up with the docs.
[10:20] Meeting end.
